incident-bot: 🚨 New incident created by Rafael Mendes
Severity: Sev2
Service: Hosted API
Symptom: p95 latency increased (chat.completions)
Detected by: latency-slo-burn (prod-us-east)
War room: #inc-1762721188
Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/ops/dashboards/latency?region=us-east

Rafael Mendes: seeing p95 jump from ~1.2s -> 3.6s in us-east over last 15m. error rate flat. anyone else seeing this / is this real user impact vs telemetry?

Sergio Costa: looking at ops dashboard now. p95 and p99 both up. p50 barely moved. looks like tail latency issue.

Allison Grant: quick check: do we trust the p95 panel? that panel is from `gateway_request_latency_ms` histogram (was changed last week). there was a bucket config change.

Rafael Mendes: good call. can someone sanity check with traces or client-side metrics?

Sergio Costa: tracing sample: https://console.redwood.ai/ops/traces?query=route:chat.completions%20region:us-east
I’m seeing some requests with long “runtime_queue_wait” spans (~1.8s) on a subset.

Sofia Ivanova: if queue_wait is up, that’s more like runtime scheduler or batching pressure than telemetry. do we have a corresponding increase in runtime saturation or kv cache evictions?

Noah Patel: pulling runtime metrics now. `runtime_scheduler_stall_seconds` looks noisy but not clearly spiking. `kv_cache_evictions_total` up ~20% but that’s within normal variance.

Allison Grant: another angle: compare with `client_observed_latency_ms` (SDK beacon) and `edge_to_gateway_latency_ms`. if those are flat, could be instrumentation bug.

Mei Lin: SDK beacon for Hosted (webhook from last 30m) shows median stable, p95 up but only ~+900ms (not +2.4s). sample size smaller though.

Rafael Mendes: so maybe real but smaller than gateway histogram suggests? hmm.

Mina Haddad: any routing changes? we had policy update in us-east earlier for model fallback preference.

Sergio Costa: router logs show increased fallback rate from model A -> model B due to “health_degraded”, but only ~3% of traffic. doesn’t line up with p95 shift.

Dylan Brooks: incident-bot reminder: please set incident_type + owner when known (can be “unknown” temporarily).

Rafael Mendes: not setting yet. still deciding whether this is runtime perf regression vs telemetry false positive.

Allison Grant: I’m suspicious of the histogram change. we changed bucket boundaries and the query is doing `histogram_quantile()` over mixed label sets. if there’s a label mismatch (e.g., `route` vs `route_name`), it can produce garbage p95.

Sergio Costa: but traces are showing real queue_wait. not garbage.

Sofia Ivanova: could be two things: 1) small real regression causing tails; 2) telemetry exaggerating it. for classification, we should choose primary symptom that’s driving IC actions.

Noah Patel: checking deploys: serving-runtime had a config flip ~40m ago in us-east only: `continuous_batching.max_delay_ms` from 8 -> 12 as part of cost tuning.

Rafael Mendes: that’s a good lead. would that increase tail latency? yes.

Sofia Ivanova: yes, higher max delay increases batching window => higher tail latency esp at low/medium load. not a “bug” per se but it’s a runtime/config-induced latency regression.

Mei Lin: timeline matches: p95 starts climbing ~10m after that flag rollout. :thinking_face:

Allison Grant: still want to fix the dashboard query, but agree this seems like actual tail latency regression driven by config.

Mina Haddad: routing wasn’t touched in that window besides the earlier policy. likely not routing.

Rafael Mendes: mitigation proposal: revert max_delay_ms in us-east to previous value. Noah can you roll back?

Noah Patel: yep. rolling back flag now for us-east canary first. ETA 5-10m to propagate.

incident-bot: @channel IC update requested: provide current status + mitigation + next update time.

Rafael Mendes: Status: investigating tail latency regression in us-east Hosted API. Suspect serving-runtime batching config change increasing queue wait. Mitigation in progress: rollback `continuous_batching.max_delay_ms` to 8ms (canary -> full). Next update in 10m.

Sergio Costa: watching p95 now. canary pool p95 already trending down (3.4s -> 2.2s). nice.

Allison Grant: ok, that’s real impact then. still opening a follow-up to fix the histogram query so we don’t overreact next time.

Rafael Mendes: agreed.

Dylan Brooks: incident-bot: please choose incident_type/subtype. options include: Latency Regression > Runtime config/regression, Latency Regression > Telemetry false positive, etc.

Rafael Mendes: Tentative classification: incident_type = “Latency Regression”; subtype = “Serving runtime config/regression (batching window)”. Owner: Serving Runtime. Contributing factor: Observability dashboard query may have overstated the magnitude.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. let’s add a note: not a code regression, config tuning gone wrong. we should add guardrails / perf-canary on tail.

Noah Patel: rollback completed to 100% us-east. p95 now ~1.5–1.7s, still slightly above baseline but improving. monitoring next 15m.

Sergio Costa: p99 down too. errors still flat.

Rafael Mendes: next steps:
1) Runtime: open ticket to add rollout guardrail for batching delay (canary + auto-revert on p95 delta) and document safe ranges.
2) Observability: validate `gateway_request_latency_ms` histogram + dashboard query; ensure route label consistency.
3) Data: Mei to pull before/after analysis (p95 delta, affected routes/models) for postmortem.
We’ll keep Sev2 open until p95 stable 30m.

Allison Grant: I’ll take #2. will post in #eng-observability with details. also might be worth adding a second “latency from traces” panel so we’re not 100% dependent on one metric.

Mei Lin: on it. will export a quick timeline and attach to postmortem stub.

incident-bot: Incident field update recorded:
incident_type: Latency Regression
subtype: Serving runtime config/regression
owner: Serving Runtime
contributing_systems: Observability (dashboard/query)

Rafael Mendes: cool. leaving classification as-is unless we find it was 100% telemetry. if p95 stays down, we can close with a short retro + follow-up tickets.
